packages.name: cli
notes: Verified project check requires every source external module to be explicitly listed in psconfig.json runtimeDependencies. Build/run additionally read node_modules/<package>/package.json and require exact name/version identity before TypeScript compilation.
Runtime dependency policy has its own SHA-256 fingerprint and is reported separately from pskernel projectIntegrity; host package versions do not alter theorem meaning.

Verified build compiles the generated TypeScript using the absolute dist/<entry>.ts path, aligning TypeScript package lookup with the emitted JavaScript runtime location. A local no-network ESM fixture gates String -> String external execution end to end.

Verified check/build/run reports now include an assurance object separating pskernel-checked definitions/theorems from trusted runtime external assumptions. Each runtime assumption records local name, ESM source, imported symbol, logical signature, and proofEvidence=false.
Human-readable verified check/build output warns when runtime external assumptions are present; --json exposes complete binding details.

DS5.6 emits one proofscript-module@2 checked-admission artifact per verified source module below dist/.proofscript/modules. Each artifact is dependency-linked by artifact integrity and replay-gated through checked core/pskernel before build acceptance.

Persistent artifacts are not yet source-skipping cache hits: a self-hashed kernel-valid artifact does not prove derivation from the current source. Trusted reuse waits for an external expected hash/lockfile or derivation certificate plus pinned base-environment identity.
moduleSources now expose both the existing canonical source/dependency cache-key integrity and moduleArtifactIntegrity; those identities intentionally serve different purposes.

CLI project resolution now consumes @proofscript/project/node for sourceRoots expansion and logical .ps/.lean module lookup; the CLI preserves PS_CLI_CONFIG_SOURCE_ROOTS at its user-facing config boundary.
DS5.5 adds project-relative `sourceRoots` configuration. Empty/unset preserves the historical entry-directory import root; configured roots replace that default search set.

Every logical import is searched across all configured roots and both .ps/.lean. Resolution requires exactly one candidate; duplicates across roots or source kinds fail with PS_PROJECT_SOURCE_AMBIGUITY instead of first-root precedence.
Verified check/build/run reports expose the absolute resolved sourceRoots alongside module/project integrity data.

DS5.4 integrates @proofscript/project BuildCache for local checked admissions. Cache keys are SHA-256 over @proofscript/module canonical JSON containing the pinned kernel descriptor, logical module name, source-kind-neutral canonical source hash, and direct dependency integrity keys.

Dependency integrity is transitive: changing a dependency changes its module key and therefore invalidates importers even when importer source is unchanged. Project integrity hashes the ordered module/integrity list.
Cache hits remain untrusted acceleration only: the final combined admissions are replayed through checked core/pskernel exactly as on a cache miss.

DS5.3 seeds each module elaboration from the pskernel-replayed checked-core metadata of its transitive dependency closure, so cross-module structures, projections, classes, and global instance synthesis match same-file behavior.

A mixed-source regression exercises Core.ps structure/class/global instance metadata from Data.lean record/projection/local-class code and instance synthesis, then runs the ProofScript entry through verified JS.

DS5.2 verified check/build/run recursively resolve logical imports from the entry source directory, topo-sort them through @proofscript/project, elaborate each module against exactly its transitive dependency admissions, then compile one combined pskernel-checked project.

Mixed-source runtime regressions cover ProofScript -> Lean -> ProofScript transitive imports and Lean -> ProofScript imports; imported ordinary definitions execute through the same verified IR/TS/JS backend.
Verified project reports expose moduleCount, deterministic moduleOrder, and per-module source kind/path/canonicalSourceHash.
Standalone verified source helpers reject imports without project context; the transitional legacy semantic lane rejects imports entirely rather than ignoring them.
DS3.3 adds a source-kind-neutral SHA-256 identity over canonical ProofScript printing of the shared parsed surface; verified and legacy check/build reports/manifests expose canonicalSourceHash.
Equivalent .ps and canonical supported .lean inputs are gated to produce the same canonicalSourceHash before semantic checking.
DS4 integration compares pskernel checked-core admission fingerprints, verified compiler IR, TypeScript, JavaScript, and .d.ts across PS -> Lean and Lean -> PS round trips.
DS4 also asserts unsupported Lean commands fail closed before checked core instead of entering a weaker semantic lane.
DS3.2 adds `psc translate <file> --to ps|lean` as a pure source frontend -> canonical AST -> target printer operation. It does not invoke verified or legacy semantic checking.
Translate requires an explicit input file and exactly one target; --verified, --json, and runtime passthrough are rejected as category errors.
Filesystem regressions cover `.ps -> canonical .lean -> canonical .ps` through the same frontend/target registries.
DS3.1 check/build/run/emit-lean select the source frontend from .ps/.lean paths while preserving the existing verified-vs-legacy pipeline choice; source kind never selects a weaker semantic checker.
Verified .lean filesystem run regression exercises Lean-subset parse -> shared elaboration -> pskernel -> checked core -> compiler IR -> TypeScript -> JavaScript -> runtime.
Build artifact stems strip the actual entry extension, so main.lean emits main.ts/main.js rather than main.lean.ts.
psc emit-lean now resolves input through the source frontend registry and output through the independent translation-target registry; it no longer hard-codes parseV061Module/lowerV061ModuleToLean.
Verified filesystem execution now also covers a generic higher-order map plus structurally recursive length over a pskernel-admitted recursive list.
CLI filesystem regression now executes a kernel-admitted recursive PsList plus structurally recursive length through emitted JavaScript and checks length(two elements) = 2.

psc run --verified now decodes arguments from verified IR types: primitive Nat/Int/Bool/String/Unit keep compact CLI forms, while supported structures/ADTs use a strict JSON ABI. Nested Nat/Int use decimal strings, ADTs use a $ctor field, and structured results are encoded back to the same JSON-safe shape.

ADT JSON inputs are rebuilt only through generated constructor exports, preserving verified runtime tags. Structure input is field-decoded according to pskernel-derived IR metadata; host JSON never becomes proof evidence.
Function-typed, unknown, unresolved type-parameter, malformed field/constructor, and unsupported dependent runtime values remain fail-closed at the CLI ABI boundary.
Verified CLI elaboration starts from the shared pskernel-admitted Lean 4.34 Init.Prelude environment and fails closed when that fixture cannot be loaded.
psc --verified uses the preferred source -> elaboration -> checked core -> erasure -> compiler IR -> TypeScript -> JavaScript architecture.
Verified mode never falls back to the legacy software checker after an elaboration/erasure error.
The legacy software path remains available without --verified only as a temporary compatibility lane while verified-core coverage expands.
CLI regression now executes a temporary verified project end-to-end through emitted JavaScript and checks Nat main(21) = 42.

packages.name: module
notes: proofscript-module@2 checked-admission payload formatVersion 1.1.0 carries checked-core codec v2, including replayable external admissions. Existing 1.0.0/codec-v1 artifacts remain readable.
Artifact verification couples payload formatVersion 1.0.0 to codec v1 and 1.1.0 to codec v2, preventing version-label downgrades from smuggling newer admission kinds.

Artifact v2 stores canonical ProofScript checked-admission JSON produced by @proofscript/checked-core. Loading verifies hashes/dependencies, decodes the closed admission payload, checks pinned kernel compatibility, then replays every admission through checked-core/pskernel.
Artifact v1 Lean4Export NDJSON remains supported unchanged for compatibility.
v2 is an untrusted persistent cache/transport. Free variables, expression/universe metavariables, and mdata are rejected by checked-core codec v1; no serialized proof bypasses kernel admission.
This closes the fake-Lean4Export blocker: ProofScript-produced modules no longer need a checked-core -> Lean4Export serializer to persist replayable admissions.

packages.name: browser
notes: Browser foundation provides cancellation-aware streaming verification through an injected verifier adapter.
Kernel/module WebCrypto wiring remains outside this foundation until the browser-safe module codec is defined.

packages.name: syntax
notes: A post-v0.7 repository extension adds `extern function local(args) : Result from "pkg" import named;` as the explicit first-order named-ESM FFI source form. The ProofScript printer preserves the full runtime binding; internal Lean lowering renders only its logical axiom view.

`psc translate --to lean` rejects modules containing extern declarations because canonical Lean cannot preserve npm/ESM runtime binding metadata; losing that metadata silently would violate dual-source semantic translation.
DS5.1 adds shared leading `import Foo.Bar` module headers to the V061 module AST. Both source frontends parse them and both canonical printers preserve them before declarations.

The bounded import header intentionally accepts exactly one logical module per line; Lean-subset imports reject semicolon spelling, while ProofScript input may accept it but canonical printing normalizes to Lean-compatible no-semicolon headers.

DS3.1 registers the completed bounded lean-subset SourceFrontend alongside proofscript in the default registry. Source extension selects only parsing/printing ownership; downstream semantic pipeline choice remains independent.

DS2 is complete for the canonical Lean subset currently emitted by the ProofScript target printer: def/theorem, structure/class/instance/inductive, records, literals/operators, fun/let/if/match, where declarations, synthetic holes, and the landed theorem tactics all parse back into the shared v0.6.1 AST.

An integrated emitted-subset gate checks ProofScript -> canonical Lean -> Lean-subset parse -> canonical Lean idempotence and canonical ProofScript equivalence across declarations, records, match, where, and theorem tactics.

DS2.2 extends the separate Lean-subset parser to canonical structure/class/instance/inductive declarations plus canonical record values, all lowering into the existing shared v0.6.1 AST rather than source-specific semantic nodes.

Canonical Lean structure/class fields are newline-delimited. Shared type parsing now has an opt-in stopAtLineBreak boundary used only by the Lean declaration frontend; ordinary ProofScript type parsing keeps its previous whitespace-application behavior.

Class and inductive parameters/constructor parameters remain explicit-only in the Lean subset because the canonical ProofScript printer cannot yet round-trip broader binder shapes there. Explicit constructor result types remain fail-closed.

DS2.1 adds a distinct fail-closed Lean-subset parser for canonical def/theorem declarations, native binders, the shared dependent type/proposition grammar, named application, literals, unary/binary terms, fun/let/if, and the landed tactic subset.
Canonical Lean named applications now round-trip grouped complex arguments without accumulating parentheses.
DS1 translation targets are explicit and separate from source frontends: target `ps` uses the canonical ProofScript printer and target `lean` uses canonical Lean lowering.
Translation target registration rejects duplicate ownership and records canonical output extensions `.ps` / `.lean` for later CLI translate integration.
DS1 canonical ProofScript printing now covers every AST shape produced by the current v0.6.1 parser and is exposed as SourceFrontend.print for the proofscript frontend.

Canonical printing normalizes formatting, declaration semicolons, grouped explicit parameters, D-call/type-call spelling, braced E-forms, and the current flat tactic sequence. It intentionally does not promise comment/whitespace preservation.

A parse -> canonical print -> parse -> canonical print regression is byte-stable across structures, classes, inductives, functions, implicit+explicit binders, if, match, where, records/instances, and theorem tactics.
Printer paths fail closed for AST binder shapes that the current ProofScript parser cannot read back, such as non-explicit class/inductive-constructor/where binders.
DS1 source-kind dispatch is now explicit: `.ps` maps to `proofscript`, `.lean` maps to `lean-subset`, and unsupported extensions fail closed.
Frontend registration rejects duplicate source-kind ownership, keeping source selection deterministic before shared semantic elaboration.
Kernel-facing tactic syntax recognizes bare `exact?` and lowers it to Lean `exact?`. Config/using modifiers are intentionally outside the accepted slice.

The type/proposition grammar now recognizes explicit dependent arrows `(x : T) -> U`, matching the v0.7 reference example `(x : Nat) -> Fin x -> Nat` and lowering directly to Lean binder-arrow syntax.
Named dependent binders are scoped in dependency analysis so the binder name is not misclassified as a local declaration dependency.
The theorem/type-position grammar now reuses the full current v0.6.1 Bool/Nat binary precedence table for +,-,*,/,%, relations, ==, !=, &&, and ||, and adds Bool literals plus unary !.
Canonical Lean lowering is split from parsing. It uses Lean 4.34 operator precedences, including =/== at 50, && at 35, and || at 30, so generated parentheses preserve the ProofScript AST.

The theorem/type-position binary grammar now includes Nat <,<=,>,>= using the shared operator precedence table. Relations bind below Nat arithmetic and above propositional `=`/arrows in the supported surface.

Type/proposition positions now parse Nat literals and the existing +,-,*,/,% precedence using the shared v0.6.1 operator table. Arithmetic binds tighter than propositional `=`, which binds tighter than arrows.
This syntax supports reference examples such as `theorem addZero(n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := ...` while leaving comparison/Boolean/general expression header syntax for later checkpoints.
Type-position syntax now has a non-associative propositional equality node. Applications bind tighter than `=`, and `=` binds tighter than arrows; lowering preserves Lean's `a = b` spelling.
Chained `a = b = c` is rejected unless explicitly parenthesized; no global textual equality rewrite is used.

Bounded `simp only [h1, ← h2, ...]` now parses an explicit rule list, including optional reverse markers and a trailing comma, while default `simp`, erasures, `*`, locations, pre/post markers, and configs remain outside the supported parser subset.
The tactic parser preserves Lean-compatible rewrite spelling for the bounded subset: `rw [h]` and `rw [← h]`; it does not introduce a ProofScript-only bare-rw syntax.
Inherited Lean `induction <local>` syntax is parsed/lowered canonically; the bounded semantic implementation uses pskernel recursors and does not introduce a second induction principle.
Inherited Lean `cases <local>` tactic syntax is parsed/lowered canonically; the bounded semantic implementation lives in elab and delegates elimination to pskernel-generated recursors.
Inherited Lean constructor tactic syntax is parsed as an ordinary theorem tactic and lowers canonically to `constructor`; no ProofScript-specific proof rule is introduced.
Inherited Lean synthetic-hole syntax ?_ is parsed/lowered for theorem tactics; ordinary executable elaboration rejects it, and the current semantic consumer is bounded refine only.
Inherited Lean tactic terms use an ordered flat tactic sequence rather than recursive continuation fields; semicolons are consumed as tactic separators only when followed by a supported tactic head.

Inherited Lean `instance` declarations now parse as named or anonymous definition-like commands with ordinary binder sequences, result type, and term body; no new ProofScript feature ownership is claimed.
Anonymous instances receive deterministic internal names for downstream metadata while canonical Lean lowering omits that generated name.
Declaration parameters preserve Lean BinderInfo categories: default, implicit, strictImplicit, and named instImplicit.
D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS remains a ProofScript-owned non-empty explicit group; native `{...}`, `{{...}}`, and named `[...]` binders remain Lean-shaped syntax.
The function alias still requires at least one D-EXPLICIT-PARAMS group, so native implicit binders alone do not satisfy the alias rule.
Canonical lowering and exact feature-ownership conformance preserve binder categories rather than translating them into TypeScript generics.
Native Lean theorem declarations are parsed as inherited command heads; only registered ProofScript parameter/separator decoration is claimed by feature ownership.
A bounded inherited Lean tactic-term parser recognizes `by exact term` and `by assumption` without registering a new ProofScript syntax exception.
Inherited Lean tactic syntax now includes a bounded `intro name; <continuation>` form; it is not registered as new ProofScript syntax.
Structure headers now reuse the shared Lean binder sequence; parameterized structures lower canonically instead of being a separate grammar.

packages.name: pretty
notes: Foundation provides compositional documents, width-aware groups/indentation, and diagnostic rendering.

packages.name: environment
notes: Platform-neutral replay turns pinned lean4export text into a pskernel Environment.
The Node subpath locates/replays the Lean 4.34 Init.Prelude fixture once and returns clones to compiler/editor clients.
Verified compilation requires the shared prelude provider and fails closed if it is unavailable; editor tooling may expose degraded empty-environment behavior separately.

packages.name: checked-core
notes: Runtime externals are replayed as ordinary non-proof-valued axioms plus separate runtime-external binding metadata. They are not Lean `unsafe` declarations: JavaScript execution is never used by pskernel, and the logical constant is opaque/uninterpreted.
Replay itself enforces the first FFI profile: at least one explicit parameter, primitive runtime parameter/result types only, no proof-valued or polymorphic external signatures.
Checked-admissions codec version 2 persists external admissions; version 1 remains readable and is forbidden from containing the new admission kind.

Checked-core codec v1 serializes closed definition/theorem/inductive/structure/class/instance admissions into versioned JSON data. It rejects free variables, expression/universe metavariables, and mdata rather than persisting unresolved elaborator state.
Decoded admissions do not become trusted declarations: callers must replay them through admitCheckedCoreAdmissions/pskernel.
Instance metadata is accepted only for pskernel-admitted definitions whose final result head is a previously admitted class; the kernel itself still sees an ordinary definition.
Class metadata is accepted only after the same single-constructor inductive validation used for structures; pskernel itself receives only ordinary inductive declarations.
Structure field-name/index/binder metadata is accepted only after validation against the constructor generated by pskernel; metadata guides source names but has no proof authority.
Checked core now replays constants and inductive declarations in admission order; inductive families are admitted by pskernel's Lean-style inductive checker.
Checked core is the single semantic boundary between elaboration and compilation.
A CheckedCoreModule is constructed only by replaying declarations through pskernel into a cloned base environment.
Compiler/erasure/editor layers may consume checked core but cannot bypass kernel admission or mutate the kernel TCB.

packages.name: meta
notes: Meta now owns bounded universe metavariables alongside expression metavariables. Simple structural universe equations are solved during elaboration, assignments are transactional with expression unification, and unresolved universe metavariables fail before kernel admission.
This is intentionally smaller than Lean Meta level unification: complex max/imax constraints that are not structurally aligned fail closed rather than being guessed.
Expr metavariables now use pskernel's real Expr and LocalContext rather than only a generic placeholder protocol.
The context records natural/synthetic/syntheticOpaque kind, creation depth, local scope, assignments, recursive instantiation, occurs checks, and kernel-backed validation once assignments are ground.
Ordinary unification never assigns syntheticOpaque metavariables; explicit assignment remains available to tactic/elaboration code.

This is intentionally not full Lean.Meta.isDefEq: level metavariables, delayed assignments, higher-order pattern unification, postponed constraints, local instance synthesis, and transparency-sensitive meta reduction remain later milestones.
First-order application-spine unification is transactional: nested metavariables such as Option ?α can be solved from expected Option Nat, and failed structural unification rolls assignments back.
This remains intentionally smaller than Lean.Meta.isDefEq; higher-order patterns, level metavariables, coercions and postponed constraints are separate milestones.

The first typeclass-resolution slice is local-only and class-aware: application elaboration may solve an instImplicit goal from the newest matching local instImplicit binder after ordinary Meta unification.

packages.name: elab
notes: Source extern signatures reuse ordinary header elaboration, are converted to non-unsafe Lean axioms plus explicit runtime-binding metadata, and are validated by the existing checked-core first-order primitive external invariant before entering the working environment.
Proof-valued extern result types are rejected at the checked-core external boundary; source syntax does not create a more permissive FFI lane.

Declaration elaboration accepts an optional checked-core seed containing already-admitted imported structures, classes, and instances. Imported metadata is reconstructed only from pskernel-validated CheckedCoreModule output, never directly from unverified source.

Imported structure/class metadata initializes record/projection and class recognition exactly like same-file metadata. Imported instances are reversed into newest-admission-first candidate order, matching the existing same-file unshift priority.

Bounded `exact?` now closes a goal using newest-first local exact hypotheses, then newest-first already-admitted zero-universe environment constants whose checked type is definitionally equal to the target.
Search is capped at 4096 environment candidates. Candidate probing is side-effect-free and final closure delegates to the ordinary `exact` transition/runtime kernel adapter.

Full Lean library search remains unsupported: no polymorphic candidate instantiation, apply-generated subgoals, solveByElim, symmetry, Iff mp/mpr candidates, unstable-name filtering, config, `using`, +all, or +grind.

Explicit dependent Pi types `(x : T) -> U` now elaborate by checking T as a type, extending the local context with x while elaborating U, then abstracting the local free variable into the kernel `forallE` body.
The current Pi slice intentionally supports one explicit default binder per arrow. Implicit/strict-implicit/instance Pi binders in type syntax remain fail-closed until required by real source.

Bool literals plus !, &&, ||, ==, and != can now appear as dependent theorem/type-position terms. They reuse the same Bool.not/Bool.and/Bool.or and bounded Nat/Bool BEq construction/checking helpers as ordinary expressions.

Bool-valued header expressions are not propositions by themselves: final declaration types still must inhabit a Sort. Typical propositions use outer propositional equality, for example `(x == y) = true`.
The syntax lowerer preserves ProofScript's established operator ordering but emits parentheses where Lean 4.34's equal precedence for `=` and `==` would otherwise change the parse.

Nat <,<=,>,>= in theorem/type-position syntax reuse the same LE.le/LT.lt construction as ordinary verified relation expressions. Header elaboration builds only the proposition; executable if-condition elaboration separately constructs Nat.decLt/Nat.decLe.

Nat literals and +,-,*,/,% in theorem/type-position expressions now reuse the same Nat constant construction and operand/result checks as ordinary expression notation; no second theorem-only arithmetic semantics exists.
Notation elaboration is split by responsibility into support, Nat, Bool, and a small dispatcher, restoring the enforced <=300-line source-shape invariant without adding an exemption.
The theorem/type-position arithmetic slice is intentionally Nat-only. General Lean overloaded arithmetic/typeclass notation remains unsupported until its Meta semantics are modeled.

Native theorem/header `=` elaborates through the real polymorphic Lean Eq constant and the shared application elaborator; operand types must unify and the completed proposition is still required to inhabit a Sort.

Type-position application arguments now elaborate as ordinary dependent terms through the shared application elaborator; only the final declared parameter/result/annotation is required to inhabit a Sort. This admits propositions such as `Eq (Nat.succ a) a` without weakening type validity.

Source equality regressions now use Lean-compatible `Eq a b` spelling, leaving the element type implicit as in Lean. Internal kernel Expr construction may still apply Eq with the explicit core type argument after elaboration.

The current type-position syntax can express named references, applications, grouping, and arrows. Numeric literals, operators, lambdas, matches, and general ordinary expression grammar in theorem headers remain future syntax work; infix propositional `=` is also not yet parsed there.

Bounded `simp only` now accepts one or more explicit Eq rules in inherited Lean list syntax and applies them in source order across repeated passes, reconstructing every change through the shared kernel-checked equality transport path.

Until Lean's discrimination-tree candidate ordering and priorities are modeled, multi-rule simp rejects pairwise structurally overlapping selected lhs patterns. This makes the accepted subset deterministic instead of silently choosing a non-Lean rule order.
Every selected direction must still strictly decrease the conservative expression-size metric; a global 64-step fuel bound remains a secondary safety guard.

The first simp slice is `simp only [h]` / `simp only [← h]` with exactly one explicit Eq proof. It repeatedly uses the kernel-checked rw transport path to a fixed point, so simplification never mutates a goal without proof reconstruction.

To guarantee termination before Lean's full simp orientation/index machinery is modeled, the selected direction must strictly decrease a conservative structural expression-size metric; non-decreasing directions fail closed.

Global @[simp] databases, multiple simp rules, theorem preprocessing, iff rules, congruence theorem indexes, dischargers, locations, simp_all, and Lean's full orientation algorithm remain unsupported.

Because Lean `rw` is `rewrite` followed by a reducible `rfl` attempt, the bounded implementation now tries to close rewritten Eq goals with the real polymorphic Eq.refl when both sides are definitionally equal. Broader reflexive relations remain outside the current rfl slice.

Bounded rw follows Lean 4.34 rewrite's core equality-transport model: inspect an Eq proof, abstract target occurrences into a motive, solve the rewritten target, then reconstruct the parent with Prelude Eq.ndrec_symm (forward) or Eq.ndrec (reverse).
The first rw slice accepts one rule in inherited Lean spelling `rw [h]` or `rw [← h]`, rewrites only exact structural occurrences in the current goal, and kernel-checks the final transport term.
Locations (`at h`), multiple rules, occurrence selectors, iff rewriting, defeq/kabstract occurrence matching, and theorem-argument synthesis beyond existing term elaboration remain fail-closed.

Global constant references now instantiate every declaration universe parameter with a fresh untrusted level metavariable. This enables ordinary elaboration constraints to specialize universe-polymorphic Prelude constants without changing pskernel.

Bounded induction supports unindexed inductives and constructs the motive by abstracting the major premise from the current target. Each branch receives all constructor fields followed by induction hypotheses for direct recursive fields, matching pskernel recursor-minor binder order.
Each induction hypothesis has the motive instantiated at its recursive field; branch proofs are lambda-abstracted over fields first and IHs second before the pskernel-generated recursor is applied.

Higher-order/nested recursive fields, indexed families, local-let majors, and surrounding locals dependent on the major fail closed until the corresponding Lean Meta generalization/recursor machinery is modeled.

Cases rejects local let scrutinees and any surrounding local whose type/value depends on the scrutinee; Lean's dependent-context substitution/generalization machinery must land before those shapes are accepted.

Bounded cases constructs an ordinary pskernel-generated recursor proof for unindexed, non-recursive inductive locals. The current goal is abstracted over the scrutinee to form the motive, and one ordered tactic goal is created per constructor.

Constructor fields are introduced only inside each branch context and branch proofs are lambda-abstracted into recursor minors. Empty inductives close the parent goal with the zero-minor recursor path.
Recursive and indexed inductives fail closed in cases until induction hypotheses, index generalization/equalities, and dependent branch contexts are modeled with Lean-compatible semantics.

Bounded constructor follows Lean 4.34 MVarId.constructor: inspect the inductive target, try constructors in declaration order, and delegate the first applicable constructor to the same apply machinery.

The current constructor slice inherits bounded apply's explicit-binder limitation; constructors requiring unresolved implicit/instance binders remain fail-closed instead of gaining a tactic-specific inference shortcut.

Bounded refine follows Lean 4.34 refineCore's key contract: a partial proof is checked against the current target and explicit synthetic ?_ holes become ordered goals whose solutions are assembled into one ordinary pskernel-checkable Expr.
Current refine intentionally differs from refine': natural _ holes, unresolved implicit parameters, and unresolved instances do not become goals; they fail closed.
The first refine slice supports a direct ?_ goal and direct D-CALL arguments such as f(?_); nested synthetic holes remain unsupported until general term-with-holes elaboration exists.

Theorem tactic elaboration consumes @proofscript/tactic's ordered goal state. exact/assumption close the main goal, intro replaces it with one child, and bounded explicit apply may replace it with multiple ordered subgoals.

Multi-goal apply assembles an ordinary kernel Expr only after all explicit premise goals are solved; result-side unification may infer explicit parameters, while implicit/instance binders remain fail-closed.
Declaration orchestration is split from value and instance elaboration; typeclass growth must stay in dedicated modules rather than expanding the command dispatcher.
Named/anonymous instance declarations elaborate as ordinary checked definitions and are registered for subsequent class-aware application synthesis.

Current global resolution searches registered instance constants after local instances. Instance goals containing unresolved metavariables are postponed and retried after later explicit/result constraints, preventing declaration order from prematurely fixing type parameters.
Parameterized instance application, priorities, outParam/semiOutParam, recursive/table-based search, imported instance indexes, and ambiguity diagnostics remain future milestones.

Applications of functions with instImplicit parameters now reuse matching local class instances from the elaboration context. Targets must be previously admitted ProofScript classes; arbitrary instImplicit types are not treated as classes.

This is intentionally not full Lean SynthInstance: priorities, parameterized/recursive search, outParam/semiOutParam, tabled resolution, ambiguity handling, and prelude instance indexing remain later milestones.
ProofScript class declarations now elaborate through the structure/inductive path and are admitted by pskernel; class-ness remains untrusted elaborator metadata, matching Lean's kernel boundary.

Acyclic where helpers now elaborate as typed local definitions and are closed into ordinary kernel let/lambda terms; dependency ordering includes term references and type annotations with lexical shadowing.
Recursive/mutual where cycles still fail closed with PS_ELAB_WHERE_RECURSION_UNSUPPORTED until they can use Lean-compatible termination elaboration.
Parameterized structures elaborate as genuine pskernel single-constructor inductives with shared parameters; constructor parameters are copied implicitly as in the existing inductive path.
Record literals for applied structures feed the admitted constructor parameter telescope before fields, and projections resolve structure identity through the applied target type.

Primitive structural recursion may carry invariant explicit parameters: every non-decreasing explicit argument must be passed as the identical local, while exactly the matched ADT parameter decreases to a direct recursive field.
Recursive calls are replaced by pskernel recursor induction hypotheses before checked-core admission; accepted definitions contain the recursor, never a self constant.
Changing an invariant argument, recursing on the original scrutinee, using arbitrary decreasing expressions, or changing recursive-call arity fails closed.
General Lean termination elaboration, multiple decreasing parameters, course-of-values/well-founded recursion, mutual recursive functions, and recursive where blocks remain later milestones.
Bounded structural recursion is elaborated by replacing self-calls on direct recursive match fields with pskernel recursor induction hypotheses; no self constant is introduced into checked core.
Recursive calls on the original scrutinee, arbitrary expressions, or non-recursive fields fail closed as non-decreasing.

Direct positive recursive inductive fields are now elaborated by making only the in-progress inductive header visible in a temporary elaboration environment; final positivity and recursor generation remain entirely pskernel responsibilities.
A negative recursive occurrence regression is rejected by pskernel's existing strict-positivity checker, not by duplicated frontend theory.
Fixed-result matches over direct recursive fields supply the pskernel recursor's induction-hypothesis binders internally while source patterns expose only constructor fields.
Verified constructor pattern matching now elaborates to the pskernel-generated recursor, not to a source-level switch.
A reduction regression checks that getOrZero (MaybeNat.some 7) iota-reduces through pskernel to 7.
Constructors are qualified as TypeName.constructor and become ordinary environment constants; existing dependent application elaboration handles constructor calls.
Record literals elaborate to applications of the pskernel-admitted structure constructor, in validated field order; dependent field types are instantiated by the constructor Pi telescope.
Dotted structure field references elaborate to kernel Expr.proj nodes whose type is checked by pskernel.
Non-parameterized v0.6.1 structures elaborate to genuine single-constructor kernel inductives with generated constructor/recursor metadata. Dependent later fields may reference earlier fields.

Verified bounded primitive == and != preserve Lean surface meaning: Nat operands use Nat.beq, Bool operands use Bool.beq, and != is Bool.not of the checked equality. Both forms have Bool type; generic BEq synthesis is still unsupported.

Verified Bool !, &&, and || elaborate through the real Lean Bool.not, Bool.and, and Bool.or constants. Any supported checked Bool expression may feed if via Eq Bool condition true plus Bool.decEq; Nat ordering keeps its proposition-native LE.le/LT.lt path.

The runtime compiler erases only already-kernel-validated forms: Nat.beq/Bool.not(Nat.beq) become nat.eq/nat.ne, Bool.not/and/or become boolean verified-IR intrinsics, and the Bool-to-Prop wrapper used by ite is removed only after admission.

The bounded verified notation subset maps Nat +, -, *, /, and % directly to Nat.add, Nat.sub, Nat.mul, Nat.div, and Nat.mod after requiring Nat operands/results. Verified TS emission preserves Lean total zero-divisor behavior for Nat.div/Nat.mod. Nat and Bool ==/!= plus Bool logic are covered; String/user-defined equality and generic BEq synthesis remain fail-closed until their typeclass semantics are implemented.
Lean-native `intro` opens a real forall goal, extends LocalContext with the exact binder type/info, elaborates the continuation against the instantiated codomain, and constructs a lambda proof.
`exact`, `assumption`, `intro`, and bounded single-premise `apply` elaborate to ordinary pskernel Expr proof terms; Kernel.addTheorem remains final authority.

Bounded apply opens exactly one explicit Pi/function premise and checks the resulting application against the original goal. Refine/constructor/cases/induction/rewrite/simp and multi-goal tactic state remain later work.
The public declaration elaborator now returns @proofscript/checked-core, re-admitted through pskernel as the stable compiler boundary.
Expected-type application/reference elaboration can solve inserted implicit constructor parameters for nullary constructors without introducing runtime arguments.
Verified match elaboration now passes admitted shared inductive parameters before motive/minors/major, matching pskernel recursor binder order for non-recursive unindexed parameterized inductives.
Constructor branch field types are obtained only after instantiating the admitted constructor parameter prefix; source patterns do not define constructor field types.

packages.name: tactic
notes: The generic refine transition replaces the main goal with the ordered holes returned by an elaboration adapter; it carries no proof authority and does not inspect kernel terms.
Tactic state now owns only the ordered open-goal list; proof/metavariable assignment is adapter-driven, matching Lean 4.34's Tactic.State versus Meta separation.
replaceMainGoal preserves trailing goals while exact/assumption close one goal, intro replaces it with one child, and apply may replace it with zero or many ordered subgoals.
The tactic package remains outside the TCB. Adapters must construct/assign ordinary proof terms that are ultimately rechecked by pskernel.
This state foundation is intentionally independent of @proofscript/elab so the elaborator can consume it without an npm dependency cycle.

packages.name: erasure
notes: Erasure lowers checked-core externals to typed VerifiedIrExternalImport entries and places their safe JS identifiers in the same runtime declaration namespace used by executable definitions.
The initial external runtime type profile is primitive function parameters/results only. Proof-valued, polymorphic, nominal, unknown, or higher-order external types fail closed.
Parameterized structures reuse pskernel InductiveInfo.numParams plus the existing inductive-parameter erasure machinery; only admitted type-level parameters become verified IR type parameters.
Structure field argument indexes include the admitted constructor parameter prefix, so erased type arguments cannot be mistaken for runtime fields.

Recursor-IH lowering now derives the decreasing runtime parameter from the erased recursor major; invariant runtime parameters are forwarded unchanged and only the major position is replaced by the recursive field.
The compiler-side self-call mapping depends on checked recursor structure and current checked-core runtime binders, not on raw source syntax.
If the recursor major is not exactly a top-level runtime parameter, the IH remains erased and any executable use fails closed.
This supports primitive structural recursion with invariant runtime parameters while general/well-founded/mutual recursion remains outside the verified compiler subset.
The self-call mapping is derived from pskernel recursor structure and checked-core binder opening, not from raw source recursion.
Direct recursive constructor fields now remain self-referential verified IR types and compile to ordinary recursive TypeScript tagged unions.
For recursive recursor applications, generated induction-hypothesis lambdas are consumed as checked compiler-internal artifacts and erased; source patterns still bind constructor fields only.
If an erased induction-hypothesis local survives in executable branch code, ordinary erased-local checks fail closed.
Constructor field names/types are derived from pskernel-generated ConstructorInfo, not trusted source-side ADT metadata.
Kernel-admitted simple structures now lower to verified nominal structure IR; constructor applications become record values and kernel projections become named field access.
Structure layout comes only from checked-core metadata that was validated against pskernel-generated constructor metadata.
Structure fields must currently all be runtime-level and independently representable; Type/Prop/dependent existential fields fail closed rather than being flattened unsafely.
Erasure consumes only kernel-admitted checked core, never source AST or the transitional software checker.
Sort/type binders become TypeScript type parameters but are erased from runtime arguments; Prop proof binders are erased entirely; runtime binders remain.
If an erased type/proof local survives in executable code, lowering fails closed.

The first executable verified-core slice supports generic functions, variables, applications, nested lambdas, lets, literals, and a tiny set of Bool/Unit constants; projections/recursors/primitive runtime calls remain later milestones.
Sort 0 / Prop binders are proof-level and erased completely; higher Sort binders become compile-time TypeScript type parameters. Proof terms whose types inhabit Prop are also erased.
Applications headed by Nat.add/sub/mul lower to verified IR intrinsics. Nat.sub remains a distinct intrinsic because JavaScript bigint subtraction does not have Lean Nat saturation semantics.
Checked ite applications over Nat LE/LT propositions lower to verified IR if nodes; the Decidable proof object is erased only after pskernel admission.
Application/ite/intrinsic lowering is isolated in app-erasure.ts so expression erasure remains below the repository source-shape ceiling.
Source-level regression locks the current boundary: simple runtime structures compile end-to-end, while dependent Type/Prop fields remain explicit fail-closed cases.
Source-level MaybeNat regression locks constructor identity across pskernel admission, checked core, verified IR, TypeScript tagged unions, JavaScript factories, and .d.ts output.

Parameterized recursor erasure now consumes the admitted recursor parameter prefix, erases those checked type arguments, and substitutes them into generic constructor field types before emitting match branch bindings.

packages.name: compiler-ir
notes: Verified IR can carry typed external named ESM imports. Import local names share the declaration value namespace, source/import names are validated, and import types use the same VerifiedIrType model as checked executable declarations.
External IR imports are runtime dependency metadata only; their presence does not constitute proof evidence or kernel admission.
Compiler IR now has a verified-core lane distinct from the transitional software-HIR lane.
Verified IR separates compile-time type parameters from runtime parameters so dependent/type binders can be erased from JavaScript while retained in TypeScript declarations.
The verified IR is runtime-oriented and intentionally does not reuse kernel Expr as code-generation IR.
Legacy software IR remains temporarily for coverage while verified-core erasure grows to structures, inductives, recursion, primitives, and effects.
Verified IR has explicit Nat/Bool runtime intrinsics so Lean runtime semantics are represented intentionally instead of inferred from TypeScript operators.
Verified intrinsic operation names and arities are defined by one typed compiler-IR contract. Validation consumes the same table, preventing backend-specific ad hoc arity assumptions.

Verified IR preserves ProofScript primitive identities (Nat/Int/Bool/String/Unit); host TypeScript types are selected only by backend-ts. This keeps runtime/ABI semantics out of the backend type representation.
Verified IR now represents Nat le/lt conditions and if branching explicitly after proposition/Decidable erasure.
Verified IR now represents nominal structure declarations, branded record construction, and field projection without carrying Lean kernel metadata into the backend.
Verified IR now has nominal inductive/constructor metadata and explicit constructor-value expressions, independent of pskernel recursor internals.
Verified IR now has explicit tagged-union match expressions with constructor-specific runtime field bindings.
Verified inductives may carry compile-time type parameters; constructor expressions may carry type arguments used only for TypeScript/.d.ts emission.
Verified structure declarations may now carry compile-time type parameters exactly like verified inductives.

packages.name: runtime
notes: Foundation implements exact bigint Nat/Int basics, saturating Nat subtraction, UInt8 normalization, and tagged constructor values; broader Lean runtime semantics remain later work.

packages.name: backend-ts
notes: The verified TypeScript emitter emits typed-IR external imports as canonical named ESM imports before generated declarations; aliases preserve the IR local name.
Backend imports consume explicit verified-IR metadata only and never infer proof assumptions from JavaScript/TypeScript packages.
The preferred backend lane now accepts verified compiler IR produced after pskernel admission and erasure.
Compile-time dependent type parameters are emitted as TypeScript generics for .ts/.d.ts while tsc removes them from JavaScript runtime code.
The backend remains untrusted: TypeScript/JavaScript emission cannot affect theorem validity or kernel admission.
The legacy software-HIR emitter remains temporarily for language coverage until verified-core lowering reaches those constructs.

Verified Nat/Bool intrinsic emission is exhaustive over the compiler-IR operation union. No catch-all fallback exists, so a newly introduced intrinsic must receive explicit backend semantics before TypeScript compilation succeeds.
Verified Nat.add/Nat.mul emit bigint arithmetic; Nat.sub emits a single-evaluation saturating expression matching Lean Nat subtraction.
backend-ts is the layer that maps semantic primitive IR types to host types: Nat/Int -> bigint, Bool -> boolean, String -> string, Unit -> undefined.

Verified structures emit as branded readonly TypeScript interfaces; constructor values carry an internal unique-symbol brand so distinct Lean structures do not collapse under TypeScript structural typing.
Verified inductives emit as unique-symbol tagged unions plus value-level constructor factories; constructor values remain nominally discriminated at runtime.
Verified ADT match IR emits a single-evaluation tagged-union switch; branch field bindings come from checked recursor minors and runtime constructor metadata.
Generic verified ADTs emit TypeScript type parameters and generic constructor factories; tsc removes those type arguments from JavaScript.
Verified generic structures emit branded TypeScript interfaces with generic parameters; tsc erases those parameters from JavaScript while preserving them in .d.ts.

packages.name: compiler
notes: Canonical verified compilation now also carries globally synthesized class dictionaries as ordinary pskernel-checked definition arguments; no compiler-specific typeclass representation is introduced.
Verified compilation now inherits acyclic local where helpers through ordinary checked-core let/lambda erasure; no compiler-specific where representation was added.
Canonical verified compilation now covers parameterized pskernel structures, record construction, and projection with TypeScript generic API preservation.

A source-level composition gate asserts nested let -> lambda(if) -> ADT match in verified IR and local higher-order calls from both match branches, preventing feature support from remaining isolated happy paths.

Canonical integration now covers higher-order generic structural recursion: map over a pskernel-admitted recursive generic list preserves TypeScript generics/function types while compiling recursor IHs to ordinary JavaScript recursion.
Compiler orchestration starts at CheckedCoreModule; it has no syntax, parser, language-checker, or elaborator dependency.
The preferred verified path is checked core -> erasure -> verified compiler IR -> TypeScript -> TypeScript Compiler API -> JavaScript/.d.ts/source map.
The compiler is untrusted with respect to theorem validity; pskernel admission has already occurred before this package runs.
The verified compiler now covers construction and elimination of non-recursive unindexed generic ADTs through kernel-admitted constructors/recursors.

The verified compiler now carries direct recursive ADTs and primitive structurally recursive functions—with invariant runtime parameters—from pskernel recursors to ordinary TypeScript/JavaScript recursion.
Canonical verified compilation now carries class dictionaries through the same structure IR/runtime representation; locally synthesized instances become ordinary checked runtime arguments.

packages.name: language
notes: Software checking has dedicated structure, inductive, match, and where modules rather than one monolithic semantic switch.
Acyclic where helpers are predeclared for local scope, type-checked with outer captures, dependency-sorted, and retained explicitly in checked HIR.
Recursive/mutually recursive where cycles fail closed until Lean-compatible termination elaboration is integrated.
Proof acceptance remains a pskernel/elaborator responsibility outside this software checker.
The executable structure subset accepts explicit named fields only; parsed implicit fields fail closed until generic structure elaboration exists.

packages.name: language-service
notes: DS6.6 cache invalidation ensures open imported-buffer edits affect subsequent importer analysis immediately; LSP refresh-all then republishes those updated diagnostics to the client.
An invalid imported module fails project composition as not-run with PS_PROJECT_ANALYSIS_ERROR rather than being misclassified as a local theorem rejection.

DS6.5 exposes source conversion through the same registered source frontends and translation-target printers used by psc translate. Conversion is syntax/printing only and carries no proof-authority claim.
DS6.4 builds completion/definition/reference data across the same checked mixed-source project closure used for semantic analysis. Imported .ps/.lean declarations can navigate across source kinds.
Cross-source reference lookup remains lexical and intentionally untrusted; it may over-approximate shadowed identifiers and never participates in elaboration or kernel admission.
Navigation caches are invalidated together with semantic analysis when any open document changes, and imported open buffers override host-provided source text.

DS6.2 composes transitive imported checked admissions and structure/class/instance metadata before analyzing the entry document. The language service consumes an injected project source host; filesystem resolution remains outside this package.

Same-document declarations now elaborate sequentially against the environment/metadata produced by earlier verified declarations, aligning editor verification with source order instead of rechecking every declaration against the original base environment.
Project-host failures fail closed with PS_PROJECT_ANALYSIS_ERROR and suppress document-level kernel verification rather than silently analyzing imports as absent.

DS6.1 snapshots carry sourceKind and analyzer parsing dispatches through the same default SourceFrontendRegistry used by psc. ProofScript and supported Lean documents therefore enter the same shared AST/elaboration/pskernel analysis path.
Document status reports sourceKind; replacement edits preserve the source kind selected at didOpen. Canonical Lean display continues to lower from the shared AST.
Project/import environment composition and cross-file definition/reference indexing remain later DS6 work; this checkpoint is source-kind routing only.
Editor analysis distinguishes parse success from kernel verification; only pskernel-admitted declarations are labeled verified.
Declaration-level proof state never fabricates tactic goals: verified theorems report closed, rejected theorems report the actual failure, and unsupported declarations report unavailable.
The service reuses the current parser/elaborator and accepts an environment factory for future project/import integration.
Completion, same-document definition, and reference lookup are lexical/declaration editor aids only; they do not participate in elaboration or kernel admission.
Theorem proof-state responses may include an initialGoal derived from the same real header elaboration used by declaration checking; a verified theorem still reports zero open goals.
Initial goal display is contextual editor information only and is not a cursor-sensitive tactic snapshot.

packages.name: lsp
notes: DS6.6 republishes diagnostics for all managed open documents whenever any managed buffer opens, changes, or closes, ensuring importers immediately reflect open dependency edits.
Refresh-all is conservative editor invalidation only; semantic caches are already invalidated by the language service, and proof authority remains pskernel.
Protocol v2 adds proofscript/translateDocument and advertises experimental.translateDocument. The request delegates directly to the language-service frontend/target registries.
Conversion returns canonical target text and extension only; the LSP does not overwrite source files or claim verification as part of translation.
Existing LSP completion/definition/reference methods now inherit DS6.4 cross-source results from the project-aware language service without adding a second transport-side symbol index.
DS6.3 wires the language-service project host to @proofscript/project/node, so editor import resolution uses the same .ps/.lean ambiguity and configured sourceRoots policy as psc.
For file:// entry documents, the LSP finds the nearest psconfig.json; absent config, it falls back to the entry directory exactly like the unconfigured DS5 source-root behavior.

DS6.1 maps `proofscript` LSP documents to the ProofScript frontend and `proofscript-lean` documents to the Lean-subset frontend. .ps/.lean URI extension fallback supports clients that preserve another editor language id.
The LSP does not decide VS Code file ownership; source-kind routing is isolated in a small transport module and forwarded to the language service.
LSP environment loading is delegated to @proofscript/environment/node so editor and compiler share the same pinned Lean 4.34 replay policy.
Every document analysis receives a clone of that admitted environment; the fixture is replayed by pskernel rather than trusted as pre-verified metadata.
If the fixture is missing or replay fails, the server falls back to an empty environment and reports the degraded editor environment through serverInfo instead of weakening proof acceptance.
Project/import environment composition remains a later language-service milestone.
The transport now exposes completion/definition/references backed by the untrusted language-service index; proof verification status remains independently kernel-derived.

packages.name: project
notes: `runtimeDependencies` config parsing accepts only exact npm package-root specifiers and exact x.y.z versions in the first FFI profile. Relative sources, package subpaths, node: builtins, semver ranges, and non-package objects fail closed.
The Node subpath centralizes psconfig sourceRoots validation, nearest-config discovery, project-relative root expansion, and exact .ps/.lean logical-module resolution for both psc and LSP consumers.
Configured source roots have no first-root-wins behavior: zero matches fail missing, multiple matches across roots/source kinds fail ambiguity.
sourceDependencyClosure exposes deterministic transitive source dependencies in build-plan order so CLI and editor composition share the same graph semantics.
DS5.1 extends the deterministic project graph with logical source modules carrying source path, source kind, and imports.
One logical module may map to exactly one source; `.ps`/`.lean` duplicates fail with PS_PROJECT_SOURCE_AMBIGUITY before semantic build.
Existing deterministic topological ordering, missing-dependency rejection, and cycle rejection are reused unchanged.
Foundation provides deterministic dependency ordering, cycle/missing-dependency rejection, and an in-memory build cache; npm/config integration remains later work.
Lean 4.34 final removed deprecated in-kernel native reduction; no NativeEvaluator/native-ir kernel extension is part of the compatibility architecture.
npm workspaces are enabled so package-name imports resolve from the single root install; the root lean-ts-kernel remains the TCB package and outer workspaces may depend on it, never the reverse.
docs/PROOFSCRIPT_ARCHITECTURE.md plus scripts/proofscript-architecture-check.mjs define and enforce the canonical verified compiler dependency direction.
The canonical integration regression now compiles multiple pskernel-admitted Nat functions, including a user-definition call, through verified IR to TypeScript/JavaScript.
The canonical verified integration regression now includes a pskernel-admitted structure whose constructor and projection lower through verified IR to branded TypeScript/JavaScript.

The canonical verified integration regression now includes an unparameterized pskernel-admitted ADT and zero-/one-field constructor values compiled through tagged verified IR to TypeScript/JavaScript.
The active language completion plan is docs/plans/05_LANGUAGE_COMPLETION.md; new language work must satisfy its source-to-kernel-to-runtime or source-to-kernel proof acceptance gates.

legacySoftwarePipeline.rule: no automatic fallback from verified-core compilation
